regressions.issue: Memory reads that the old text bound to variables (_95 = mem[X], _103 = mem[X + 32]) are now inlined, and a uint104 read prints as the 13-byte slice mem[X + 19 len 13]. Lines with 'len 13]' 105 -> 121, uint104(_N) 57 -> 41. Values are unchanged.
regressions.rule: Print the low n bytes of a word as uintN(mem[X]), not as mem[X + 32 - n len n]. Keep a memory read bound to a variable when its address expression is long and it is used more than once.

improvements: Free pointer resolved: every call is named (60 call sites showed a memory slice as the name), call args decoded, most event data now values, 98 bubbled reverts printed as revert with ext_call.return_data, custom errors given as selectors with args. In unknown8a3f9a8e (forceValidatorExit) the copy loop over an empty uint64[] is gone; it now passes an explicit zero length. unknown96c4d514's early 'return 0' is merged into one return after 'if min(..):'. P6 63-digit words 85 -> 0 (whole bytes). Text 5% smaller.
notes: Diff of 5.9k lines (reordering included), with about 1,000 lines added and 1,700 removed per function. Reviewed by structure: per-function counts of whiles, calls, reverts, logs, storage writes and returns. Count changes traced: unknown8a3f9a8e (while 2->1: zero-trip copy of new uint64[](0); revert 30->29: a dead Panic(65) on a now-constant pointer; no call lost, the extra count was a call.data line), and unknown96c4d514 (return 2->1: early return merged, log now inside 'if min(..)' as before). A dropped mem[64] update before the end of unknown96c4d514 is unobservable, and 'mem[mem[64]]' reads there are correct.
summary: No semantic regression. Calls are all named now and revert data are clean. A minor readability loss: 16 lines inline memory reads (uint104 shown as 13-byte slices) that were variables before.
